frame_88.jpg.note: Tiny, rigid, evenly spaced game-piece figures stand on a flat, untextured parade ground. They are lined up in toy-soldier ranks. They have no cast shadows or weight. Cannon and shot piles are blocky.

frame_36.jpg.note: The crowds are dark-red specks packed into perfect rectangles, like wargame blocks or ant swarms. Individuals are unreadable. The few lone figures are stick-like. The sandy ground has no grounding contact.

frame_80.jpg.note: Detailed ruined walls make the figures look like plastic dolls pasted in. They are stiff and glossy, with simplified faces and uniform poses. Their scale is slightly off and their contact shadows are weak. Their coats are flat colour blocks with no wool texture.

frame_14.jpg.note: Same frame as frame_88: tiny, rigid, evenly spaced toy-soldier figures on a flat plain with no real grounding.

frame_24.jpg.note: Same frame as frame_36: massed specks in perfect rectangular blocks that read as game units, not men.

frame_15.jpg.note: The 1943 sailors and soldiers are smoother and better proportioned, with a plausible mix of uniforms and some action poses. They still look glossy and plastic, with simplified faces and drab flat clothing. The cobbles lack real contact shadows. They look like game or CG avatars pasted into a photoreal street, not like real people.
